title: Browse Medicare Advantage plans
summary: Overview of UnitedHealthcare Medicare Advantage (Part C) plans, including plan types, costs, eligibility, enrollment periods, and dental, vision and hearing benefits.

atoms.title: What Medicare Advantage plans are
atoms.question: What are Medicare Advantage plans?
atoms.text: Medicare Advantage (Part C) plans offer all the benefits of Original Medicare, many with extras like dental, vision, and hearing benefits. Most include prescription drug coverage.

atoms.title: Features of UnitedHealthcare Medicare Advantage
atoms.question: Why choose a UnitedHealthcare Medicare Advantage plan?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare describes itself as America's most chosen Medicare Advantage brand. Its plans may include monthly premiums as low as $0, $0 annual physical exams, lab tests and preventive care, rewards for healthy activities, a large provider network including doctors and specialists, and $0 copays for virtual medical and mental health visits. Members also get the UCard, which opens doors to a network of Medicare Advantage providers and rewards for healthy activities.

atoms.title: Medicare Advantage plan types offered
atoms.question: What types of Medicare Advantage plans does UnitedHealthcare offer?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare Medicare Advantage plans include Health Maintenance Organization (HMO) plans, Preferred Provider Organization (PPO) plans, Private Fee-for-Service (PFFS) plans, and Special Needs plans (SNPs). Not all plans are available in all areas.

atoms.title: Medicare Advantage premium and deductible
atoms.question: What are the premium and deductible costs on a Medicare Advantage plan?
atoms.text: A monthly premium is a fee you pay to the plan for coverage, and some Medicare Advantage plans have a low or even $0 monthly premium. You may still need to pay a premium for Part B coverage. The annual deductible is the amount you pay out of pocket for health care before your plan begins to pay; most Medicare Advantage plans only have a prescription drug deductible.

atoms.title: Copayment versus coinsurance
atoms.question: What is the difference between a copay and coinsurance?
atoms.text: A copayment (copay) is a set amount you pay for a covered medical service or prescription drug; for example, some plans might charge a $40 copay each time you see a specialist. Coinsurance is a percentage of the total cost for a covered medical service or prescription drug. You pay the coinsurance and your plan pays the remaining amount.

atoms.title: Who can enroll in Medicare Advantage
atoms.question: Who is eligible for a Medicare Advantage plan?
atoms.text: Most people become eligible for Medicare coverage when they turn 65 or have a qualifying disability or medical condition. Anyone who is eligible for Medicare coverage can enroll in a Medicare Advantage plan if they live in the plan service area.

atoms.title: When to enroll in Medicare Advantage
atoms.question: When can I enroll in a Medicare Advantage plan?
atoms.text: You can enroll when you first become eligible, in your Initial Enrollment Period (IEP). If you already have Medicare coverage and want a different plan type, you can change during the Annual Enrollment Period (AEP), October 15 to December 7; the Medicare Advantage Open Enrollment Period (MA OEP), January 1 to March 31; or a Special Enrollment Period (SEP) for qualifying life events, with dates that vary.

atoms.question: Does a UnitedHealthcare Medicare Advantage plan include dental?
atoms.text: A UnitedHealthcare Medicare Advantage plan may include dental benefits, which provide coverage for dental services like cleanings, fluoride, fillings, crowns, root canals and more.

atoms.title: Vision and hearing benefits in Medicare Advantage
atoms.question: Does a UnitedHealthcare Medicare Advantage plan include vision and hearing?
atoms.text: A UnitedHealthcare Medicare Advantage plan may include a $0 vision exam; vision services help protect your eyesight and may save you money on eyewear. It may also include a $0 routine hearing exam plus savings on thousands of hearing aids.

atoms.title: Member recommendation and U.S. News recognition
atoms.question: How do members rate UnitedHealthcare Medicare Advantage?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare reports that 4 out of 5 members recommend its Medicare Advantage coverage, based on Human8, May 2025. It also states it was named a Best Insurance Company for Medicare Advantage 2026 by U.S. News & World Report two years in a row, based on 2025 and 2026 analysis of all Medicare Advantage plan ratings from CMS and enrollment data.
